analysis.title: GS US TMT .. bounce back
key_insights: NDX broke a 4-week losing streak, closing up ~350 bps on the week. Semis/SOX rose ~800 bps, the best week since early August. Both NDX and SOX still closed below their 200-day moving averages on Friday.
Nvidia had its biggest week of underperformance relative to Semis since 2008 and is down 12% YTD. Strength in AMD and the ASIC ecosystem was the short-term reaction to unexpected NVDA headlines.
US Financial Conditions rose to their tightest level in ~18 months after another hotter CPI print. The 10-year yield is back at 5.15% and oil is near $96/brl.

Callahan attributes last week's strength mainly to cleaner positioning (GS PB data showed covering via macro products) and rotation into Defensives, Big Tech (including AMD and AVGO) and Low Vol names.

Callahan sees relatively little consensus in the market apart from a receptive tilt toward the Hyperscalers. Debate centers on where the AI/Semi cycle stands, what is priced in, and whether this is a bear-market bounce or a forming bull market.
Software dispersion has picked up, including within Cyber and Data Infra. Internet has become squeezy and hard to trade, with some value interest emerging.

NVDA market cap is back below $4trn and now matches MSFT's. MDB, MSFT, DELL and TSM are testing their 50-day moving averages to the downside. ZS has been lower on 12 of 14 days. EBAY and ETSY are up 6 of 7 weeks. Staples, Low Vol and Pharma continue to rally strongly. CMCSA and CHTR are 20-35% off their lows.

NVDA reports Tuesday 11/17 after the close. Its 14-day RSI is 24, the lowest since 2019, and it trades at 11x NTM P/E. Expected focus: Vera Rubin momentum, 2027+ visibility, gross margins and capital allocation.
DIS reports Tuesday 11/17 before the open. The stock is re-testing the $120s level that has capped it for ~4+ years. Focus is on strategic initiatives into 2027+.

PANW reports Wednesday 11/18 after the close. The stock fell on 9 of its last 12 prints on T+1, trades in the low ~$300s (~$100 below YTD highs), and sentiment is upbeat. Focus is on signs of AI uplift as it laps the CyberArk and Chronosphere acquisitions in 1Q'C27.

INTU reports Thursday 11/19 after the close. It has not closed above its 200-day moving average in more than a year, and inbound interest is very low. Investors want evidence that new initiatives are working.

AAPL versus NDX is approaching its highs even though bear points from Apple's recent earnings (Services deceleration, gross margin headwinds, AI server-side inference costs) have not weighed on the stock. SPX ex-AI has outperformed SPX over the last year and was more resilient in last week's sell-off.

GS Macro Outlook for 2027: global growth of 2.8%, with lower energy prices and strong AI capex outweighing tighter financial conditions and more neutral fiscal policy. Risks are tilted to the downside: renewed Iran escalation, large fiscal deficits (especially France), and AI capex disappointment. There are early signs that AI is weighing on the job market.

Top client inbounds: sustainability of the Tech/AI bounce, memory stack rankings (HDDs, DRAM, NAND), whether people are long or short AI/Semis, new Internet ideas (OTAs, UBER, NFLX, APP), the NVDA print setup, why AMAT and CSCO fell so much T+1, and META versus MSFT.
Key events this week: Fed Chair Warsh speech Monday 11/16 at 1pm ET, US Retail Sales Tuesday 11/17, FOMC Minutes Wednesday 11/18, MSFT Ignite, and the TTWO GTA VI launch Thursday 11/19.

sector_views.rationale: SOX rallied ~800 bps on the week but remains below its 200-day. Debate continues over quality, stable-gross-margin semis versus higher-beta areas such as EMS, Memory and Neoclouds.
Dispersion has picked up, including within Cyber and Data Infra, and there is no clear theme across the charts that look surprisingly strong.
The group is squeezy and hard to trade, with some value interest emerging.
The one area with a broadly receptive consensus tilt.
These groups continued to rally strongly and were part of last week's intra-market rotation.

earnings_insights: NVDA reports Tuesday 11/17 after the close. No estimates are given in the note. The stock trades at 11x NTM P/E with a 14-day RSI of 24. The chart in the note shows F'28 (~C'27) GAAP EPS revisions against the stock price.

DIS reports Tuesday 11/17 before the open. No estimates are given. Focus is on strategic initiatives into 2027+ (cruise fleet expansion, theme park capital investment, theatrical pipeline, Spring 2027 Disney+ integration of merchandise and interactive features).
PANW reports Wednesday 11/18 after the close. No estimates are given. The stock was lower on T+1 after 9 of the last 12 prints.
INTU reports Thursday 11/19 after the close. No estimates are given. Focus is on Intuit Intelligence, QuickBooks industry verticals and broader Consumer touchpoints.
Other earnings this week: BIDU, XPEV (11/16 pre), JD, TME (11/17 pre), DLB (11/17 post), Tencent (11/18 pre), KLIC (11/18 post), BABA, PDD, Walmart (11/19 pre), ESTC, KEYS (11/19 post).
